correctness.rationale: The two-parameter objective is explicit; Gaussian rearrangement uniquely fixes the center. A strict single crossing of two exponential-moment elasticities determines the global width. A quantile-integral identity establishes strict convex order and thereby exact nonasymptotic cube-root coefficients. Small/large budget limits are derived from Taylor and essential-supremum Laplace laws. The proof covers every positive budget and Gaussian scale; 6,232 supplementary checker tests and high-precision boundary checks passed, without being treated as infinite proof.

value.rationale: The exact width addresses a concrete ecological tradeoff: floral display intensity diminishes when a finite flower-production budget is distributed over longer phenological windows, while pollinator exposure rises. Unique optimal timing and sharply bounded cube-root scaling make an actionable analytic benchmark; the upper/lower bound factor is only (4/3)^(1/3), with both constants proved optimal. The result depends on the whole positive-parameter family, not an arbitrary numerical slice. Biological extrapolation is expressly withheld.
